title: TSMC overseas fabs see profit flip in 1H26, Arizona surges 663% YoY
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

TSMC’s overseas manufacturing strategy reached an inflection point in the first half of 2026, as all four foreign subsidiaries generated a combined NT$58.53 billion in profit, up 215.4% year on year. The standout was TSMC Arizona, whose profit surged 662.8% to NT$36.07 billion, exceeding 60% of the overseas total and overtaking Nanjing as the company’s largest foreign earnings contributor.

The performance suggests that TSMC’s geographic diversification is beginning to produce operating leverage. Arizona’s first fab, running 4-nanometer technology, is benefiting from strong demand for AI and high-performance computing chips, customer interest in US-based supply, and improving production efficiency. Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing also moved from a first-half 2025 loss to a NT$1.68 billion profit, while the established Nanjing and Shanghai operations remained profitable.

Still, the headline growth rate comes from a low comparison base and should not obscure rising costs. Arizona’s second-quarter profit declined 8.2% sequentially as depreciation and expansion expenses increased. TSMC has warned that overseas expansion will dilute companywide gross margin by several percentage points. The results therefore validate overseas manufacturing commercially, but the durability of returns will depend on utilization, pricing, subsidies, execution, and whether AI demand remains strong enough to absorb an expanding global capacity base.
